instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each legislative agent to file, with each updated registration statement, a statement of expenditures.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B) (2025); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(D) (2025)
instantiated_cells.justification: Updated registration statements are due by the last day of January, May, and September each year, and expenditure statements must be filed with those updates.
The statute sets three annual filing dates (last day of January, May, and September) for updated registrations that include the expenditure statement.
The only periodic filing dates specified are January, May, and September (three times per year), not quarterly.
No monthly expenditure reporting cadence is specified; filings occur on three specified dates each year.
The statute requires updated filings three times per year, not twice per year.
The required expenditure statements are tied to triannual updated registrations rather than an annual-only filing.
The statute specifies triannual filing on the last day of January, May, and September and does not establish another periodic cadence.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(B)(1) (2025); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(C) (2025)
instantiated_cells.justification: Legislative agents must report the total amount of expenditures during the period, and employers must report their total expenditures for the period.

When thresholds/conditions apply, the statement must list recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client for expenditures to specified officials or for meals over $50.
The law mandates discrete fields (recipient, amount, description, date, legislation/client) for reportable expenditures, which is an itemized reporting format.
Expenditures include gifts and items of value such as entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and reportable expenditures must be briefly described in the statement.
For reportable expenditures, the filer must include the specific items of legislation, if any, for which the expenditures were made.

Updated registration statements list specific bills or resolutions, and expenditure itemization must identify the specific items of legislation for which an expenditure was made, supporting inclusion of specific bill identifiers.

The statute requires a brief description and separate treatment for meals/food-and-beverage reporting, but it does not mandate categorical breakdowns by expense type (e.g., travel, entertainment) across all expenditures.
The statute requires linking expenditures to specific items of legislation (if any), not aggregating or reporting expenditures per issue area.
Section 101.73 specifies reporting about expenditures to covered officials and related legislation/client, but does not require listing general issues.
The expenditure statement requirements do not include a general subject-matter field (as opposed to the separate registration statement’s 'type of legislation' description).
Section 101.73 governs expenditure statements and does not require the legislative agent’s name or business address to be included in the expenditure statement itself.

The expenditure statement must identify the client on whose behalf an expenditure was made, but it does not require listing all principals/clients generally beyond those tied to each reported expenditure.
The expenditure statement requirements do not call for reporting the employer/principal’s address or other contact information.
No requirement in the expenditure statement provisions calls for describing the principal’s business or nature of business.
The statute’s expenditure statement provisions require reporting expenditures and related details, not lobbying contacts or communications.
While the statement may identify specific legislation related to an expenditure, it does not require stating a position (support/oppose) on that legislation.

The statute expressly excludes 'compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of 'expenditures' for employer statements, and it does not otherwise require compensation reporting on the expenditure statement.
Expenditure statements are required, but compensation is excluded from employer expenditure totals and no provision requires reporting compensation by payer.
The statute excludes 'expenses of maintaining office facilities' from reportable 'expenditures' for employer statements, indicating indirect/overhead costs are not included.
Covered 'expenditures' are defined as made to or for the benefit of specified officials or staff, without extending the scope to household/immediate family members of those officials.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because the statute specifies a triannual cadence and no alternative 'other' cadence, there is no other specification to provide.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text does not state whether a 'zero' expenditure statement must be filed when no reportable expenditures occur during the period; §101.73 mandates filing but does not address no-activity situations explicitly.
